positions.name: OwnedVsRentedIntelligence
positions.frame: what separates owned intelligence from rented intelligence, and which layer of the stack is the asset one actually keeps?
positions.why: Both statements are unhedged present-tense copular claims built as antitheses — 'Owned' against 'rented', 'commodity' against 'asset you keep' — and the second completes the first's distinction by locating the durable thing in perspective rather than substrate. Read together they hold one directional stance: the value appeal is to self-origination (keeping one's own perspective), performed in matched parallel clauses rather than argued step by step. The set carries no internal tension; the two clauses are the same contrast at two grains (what intelligence is vs. where the asset sits).

placements.title: The durable asset is the perspective you keep, not the substrate you rent
placements.frame: When intelligence is assembled on someone else's substrate, which part of it does the owner actually keep — and what is merely rented back to them?
placements.why: The document's only position, OwnedVsRentedIntelligence, holds two unhedged copular antitheses (src-2, src-3) that together state a directional claim beyond their own words: ownership of intelligence is a distinction in kind, and the layer that survives commoditization is perspective rather than substrate. That is a subject future envelopes can keep feeding (it is a positioning thesis, not a measurement or one-time event), so it clears the narrative grain test. The supplied graph structure is empty — no existing leaf, hub, or stratum — so there is nothing to reuse and nothing to sit under; this is the foundational case for a standalone mint.

unconnected.why: No existing strata exist, and this response places a single narrative resting on a single position; minting a stratum to group one member would encode no cross-graph relationship yet. The grouping is left to accrue when a second narrative or position on owned-versus-rented intelligence arrives.
